title: Stress run scrub + short-seq latency spikes (weekly sync)
content:
Meeting: Performance & Benchmarking sync (weekly) - Stress run scrub
Date: 2025-11-12
Host: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya, Luca, Priya, Samir, Jordan (+ async: Ayesha, Ben)
Duration: 45m

Objective: quick triage of the last two smoke/stress runs, capture anomalies, agree on short-term experiments before next large-scale run. Focus: short-sequence latency spikes, throughput plateau at ~3k QPS in canary, KV-cache miss rate increase during rolling deploys.

Summary / TL;DR
- Observed repeatable 30–120ms tail latency spikes for short seqs (<=32 tokens) on the new kernel build (k8s-worker-3). Spikes correlated with GC-like CPU jitter on host and with occasional worker process restarts (OOM?).
- Throughput stop-gap: sustained throughput plateau near 3k QPS on 8xA100 pool under mixed workload (long+short). Hypothesis: batching timer misfire + batch size cap hitting too early for mixed sequences.
- KV cache miss rate jumped from 2.4% -> 9.8% during canary rollout (2025-11-10), coincident with config change: prefix-eviction-window lowered from 10m->2m (intended) but eviction code path had edge-case empty-key bug.
- Action items: short debugging list + owners (see below). We will NOT promote the current kernel build to prod until stability checks complete.

Run notes (detailed)
- Run: nightly-stress-2025-11-11 (canary group: c3, workers: k8s-worker-1..4)
  - Config: mixed workload: 60% short (<=32), 30% medium (33-256), 10% long (>256); model: llama-13b-quant-v2; batching: enabled, max-batch=64, batch-delay-ms=12.
  - Observed: median latency ok (22ms for short), p95/p99 shows spikes: p95=85ms, p99=210ms on k8s-worker-3 only.
  - CPU profile: intermittent user CPU microspikes; ps shows occasional process restart (worker PID rotated). No OOM logs in kube, but container restart count increased by 1 during window.

- Run: throughput-smoke-2025-11-12 (8xA100 dedicated pool)
  - Config: synthetic clients ramp to 6k QPS; steady-state target 4k QPS; batching tuned to favor larger batches for long sequences.
  - Observed: plateau at ~3.1k QPS; tokens/sec saturates while GPU utilization sits ~86%. NVLink memory bandwidth not at max. Batch histogram: lots of small batches for short seqs despite config.
  - Hypothesis: client-side shaping + server-side batch timer interplay causing premature flushes. Also examine kernel switch for attention optimized path introduced in PR#4567.

- Canaries & KV cache exploration
  - Event: 2025-11-10 canary roll changed prefix-eviction-window -> 2m to reduce memory pressure (Jira INF-3129). After rollout, cache-miss spiked.
  - Logs show frequent prefix eviction calls and a retry path that computes key length; edge case: zero-length key (rare) triggered full-prefix invalidation. Looking at code in github PR 4542 (cache eviction refactor).

Immediate hypotheses (ranked)
1) Kernel change (PR#4567) introduced a synchronization point that increases jitter at low-latency short seq code path. Repro on k8s-worker-3 correlates with that host running special kernel build.
2) Batch timer misconfiguration combined with mixed workload causes many small batches; timer threshold of 12ms too low under certain jitter -> flushes before KV warmup for short sequences.
3) Cache eviction bug (zero-length key) causes transient mass invalidation leading to more model context recompute and higher CPU overhead. Explains miss jump during canary.
4) Underlying host node (k8s-worker-3) has noisy neighbor activity (backup job?) leading to scheduling jitter. Need host-level perf counters to confirm.

Evidence / Artifacts examined
- Flame graphs (attached clip links in slack) for p99 spikes show short spikes in read syscall + kernel sync.
- dmesg from k8s-worker-3 shows repeated I/O scheduling congestion events around timestamps.
- Batch histograms show large proportion of 1-2 item batches during the plateau period.
- KV cache sampling shows prefix invalidation bursts aligning with the canary window.

Short-term experiments (next 48-72h)
- E1 (Priya): Re-run stress on k8s-worker-3 with kernel build rolled back to prior known-good and compare p99 distribution. Output: collection of traces + restart counts. Deadline: 2025-11-14.
- E2 (Samir): Temporarily increase batch-delay-ms from 12 -> 25 for canary group and run throughput-smoke. Measure batch size distribution and throughput. If plateau disappears, suggests timer interplay. Deadline: 2025-11-13.
- E3 (Luca): Add extra guard in prefix-eviction to skip zero-length keys; patch on canary only. Also add verbose counters for eviction events. Quick PR and deploy to canary. Deadline: 2025-11-13.
- E4 (Jordan): Host-level investigation on k8s-worker-3: collect perf counters (cpu-cycles, context-switches, iowait) and check for cron/backup jobs. Coordinate with infra. Deadline: 2025-11-13.
- E5 (Maya): Run isolated short-seq-only workload against same pool to confirm whether mixed workload is necessary for behavior. Deadline: 2025-11-14.

Action items (owners + tickets)
- Do not promote kernel build KERN-2025-11-06 to prod. (Owner: Maya) -> Ticket: INF-3174.
- Priya to run rollback comparison and upload traces to confluence. (Owner: Priya) -> Ticket: INF-3180.
- Samir to test increased batch-delay and post histograms + perf. (Owner: Samir) -> Ticket: INF-3181.
- Luca to hotfix eviction guard and add counters, open PR (canary-only). (Owner: Luca) -> PR/Branch: fix/eviction-guard-2025-11; Ticket: INF-3129 follow-up.
- Jordan to collect host perf and coordinate with infra for maintenance window if needed. (Owner: Jordan) -> Ticket: INF-3182.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal)
- If E2 fixes plateau, long-term: consider auto-adjusting batch-delay based on workload mix telemetry. Add to Optimize backlog.
- Cache eviction: if guard required more widely, may need short-term config flag to control eviction aggressiveness during rollouts.
- Consider adding a per-host watchdog that gates kernel promotion based on p95/p99 regression tests in staging.
- Need a small synthetic workload that mirrors product mix for future smoke runs rather than synthetic uniform distributions. TODO: define mix by product team.

Next sync: 2025-11-14 async updates; synchronous follow-up only if E1/E2/E3 produce inconclusive results or regression persists.

Appendix / raw snippets (cut-and-paste from logs)
- sample log (k8s-worker-3):
  [2025-11-11T03:12:17Z] worker[pid=21457] restart detected, reason: signal 9
  [2025-11-11T03:12:17Z] model-serving: flushing batch id=3921 size=1 delay=12ms
  [2025-11-11T03:12:17Z] kv-cache: eviction prefix len=0 (unexpected) -> full-prefix invalidation

- quick checklist for next run:
  - include kernel-control runs (prev/next) on 2 hosts
  - capture per-batch trace with trace_id tagging
  - enable eviction counters and short TTL on one canary route

If anything else observed, drop notes in #perf-debug; I'll keep updating this doc with results and will attach graphs to the confluence page.

-- Maya
